Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Oil was on track for the first weekly gain this month as attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East raised concerns escalating hostilities could disrupt exports.
Brent traded near $96 a barrel and was up 4.3% this week, while West Texas Intermediate was around $86. Tehran-backed Houthi militants attacked Saudi Arabia’s Jazan refinery on the Red Sea, temporarily halting some operations, after targeting its Ras Tanura hub in the Persian Gulf earlier this week.

Global equities extended their recovery into a second straight day as buyers returned after weeks of volatility in the artificial intelligence trade. Treasuries fell as gains in equities sapped demand for haven assets.
MSCI Inc.’s Asia Pacific equities gauge climbed 1.4%, building on a rebound that began on Wall Street Wednesday after the Nasdaq 100 Index briefly slipped into bear-market territory. Gains in US equity-index futures signaled the advance may continue when Wall Street returns for a shortened session following the Thanksgiving holiday.

Treasuries fell in light trading as the market reopened after the Thanksgiving holiday, with gains in Asian equities damping demand for haven assets.
Yields climbed at least four basis points across the curve, with the rate on benchmark 10-year notes up five basis points to 4.91%. A tentative recovery in risk appetite lured investors away from the safety of US government bonds, as regional shares extended a rebound following weeks of volatility in the artificial intelligence trade.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Copper extended its rebound from an 11-month low alongside technology stocks in Asia, as risk appetite returned across markets after weeks of volatility fueled by concerns over the artificial intelligence trade.
The red metal rose as much as 4.4% to trade above $12,300 a ton on the London Metal Exchange, putting the market on track for the first weekly increase since early October. The technology sector in Asia was among the biggest gainers on Friday, while US equity-index futures also climbed.

Save
Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
South Korean authorities will meet financial industry leaders Monday to assess recent market conditions following the central bank’s rate hike, with the country’s stock market stabilization fund also likely to come up, according to the Financial Services Commission.
The gathering is expected to be attended by the chairmen of the country’s five major financial holding companies, heads of industry associations and financial regulators, FSC spokesman Lee Dong Hoon said. The stabilization fund is not a main agenda item, and the meeting could be postponed depending on participants’ schedules, he added.

Save
Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Australia adopted a law requiring liquefied natural gas exporters to reserve as much as a fifth of their supply for the domestic market.
Legislation introduced by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s Labor government requiring major LNG exporters including Shell Plc, ConocoPhillips, Woodside Energy Ltd. and TotalEnergies SE to ensure more gas is available for Australian consumers passed the House of Representatives early on Friday. The obligation will kick in Jan. 1, 2028.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Gold rose as a tentative recovery in technology stocks and a weaker US dollar offset the prospect of interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.
Bullion climbed as much as 1.7% to near $3,627 an ounce, on track for a weekly gain after rebounding from a 15-month low two days ago. Asian stocks advanced for a second day, extending a rally following weeks of volatility in the artificial intelligence trade, while a gauge of the dollar fell 0.1%, making bullion priced in the US currency cheaper for most buyers.

item.title: How Volatility is Undermining the Carry Trade
item.description: The carry trade, in which investors borrow in currencies like the yen, euro, and dollar, is becoming harder to navigate after delivering strong returns earlier in the year.
